title: Headwise Dynamic Scale Adapter for Streaming INT8/FP8 Paths
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: reduce per-token streaming decode latency and overall throughput cost by avoiding repeated dequant/quant overhead and by enabling per-head scaling adjustments. Implement a headwise dynamic scale adapter and a fused attention kernel that operates in the quantized domain for hot attention heads while routing cold or unstable heads to mixed-precision (FP16/FP32) paths.
background: Observed: for streaming decode workloads, repeated small-token prefill+decode cycles expose dequantization overheads and poor per-head dynamic range handling in INT8/FP8 pipelines. Current kernels dequantize whole tensors back to FP16 before attention, which adds ~6-12ms per token at typical batch sizes for our 8xA100 pools. Existing adaptive fallback is coarse-grained (per-layer) and causes unnecessary quality regressions.
proposal_summary: 1) Add a lightweight headwise scale estimator run during KV write to maintain per-head quant ranges. 2) Implement a fused headwise-scaling attention kernel that consumes INT8/FP8 key+value buffers and applies scaling in-kernel to produce attention scores without full dequant round-trip. 3) Update scheduler to prioritize microbatches that contain 'hot' heads and pre-warm KV caches selectively. 4) Provide runtime flags to control head thresholding and enable safe rollback to mixed-precision paths.
design_decisions: Headwise scale retained as 8-bit per-head exponents (compact representation) to limit memory blowup.
Prefer in-kernel scaling over pre-dequant to reduce memory traffic and synchronization points.
Use a conservative thresholding policy: head marked 'hot' only after >=3 consecutive tokens above activity metric to avoid thrashing.
Fallback path is mixed-precision (FP16) per-head rather than layer-level to preserve quality on problematic heads.
Expose two knobs: activity_threshold (float) and hot_head_min_run (int) for tuning per-customer workload.
implementation_notes: Split work across three PRs: 1) telemetry+metrics for head activity; 2) runtime data-structures for head scales and compact storage; 3) fused attention kernel + scheduler integration. Kernel implementation will live under runtime/ops/attention/quant_fused_hwscale and be guarded behind feature flag EXPERIMENTAL_HEADWISE_QUANT.
progress_updates: 2025-02-10: Spike completed. Microbenchmarks show fused in-kernel scaling reduces dequant traffic by ~42% on a 175B decoder-only model with 2048 context.
2025-02-18: Prototype kernels integrated in local runtime build. End-to-end streaming test harness demonstrates 9-14% median token latency reduction on 1-token emission workloads.
2025-02-25: Added compact per-head scale serialization to KV store. Extra memory cost measured: +0.6% on average for Llama-like models.
2025-03-02: Safety tests underway. Discovered edge case where very low-activity heads mis-calibrate after long idle periods; added decay-based rescaling to mitigation branch.
2025-03-05: Canary plan drafted; awaiting PR reviews for kernel and scheduler components. Perf dashboards created.
perf_benchmarks: Benchmark setup: 8xA100, fp16 baseline, model: rwi-13B-decoder, batch=1 streaming, seq=2048, microbatch=1
Baseline median token latency: 38.2 ms (fp16 path with dequant round-trips)
With headwise fused quant kernel: 32.8 ms median token latency (-14.2%)
Throughput improvement on long sequences (microbatch aggregated): +1.5x effective tokens/sec compared to baseline INT8 with layer-level quant fallback
Cost reduction estimate: ~17% GPU token-cost reduction in our hosted traces (heavy streaming customers) when enabled with conservative knobs.
Quality: Perplexity delta on eval set: +0.003 relative (within noise) when thresholding set conservative; rare spikes observed if threshold too aggressive.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/integration tests for headwise scale estimator and decay behavior added and green.
Kernel PR passes CI/SMOKE and shows no numerical regressions vs FP16 beyond tolerances defined in runtime-1.23 QC matrix.
End-to-end streaming latency improvement reproducible on our canary cluster with stable quality metrics (no more than 0.01 perplexity regression for canary workload).
Feature flag for EXPERIMENTAL_HEADWISE_QUANT exists and default is off for existing customers.
Canary rollout plan and automatic rollback on quality/latency regressions documented.
Memory overhead <= 2% for common model families during canary.
A/B dashboards configured: token latency, tail latency (p95/p99), perplexity, cost-per-1M-tokens.
Runbooks updated for edge-case mis-calibration and TTL-based decay.
Benchmarks reproducible with supplied scripts in links section.
Security review N/A but performance knobs audited for DoS surface (throttling limits applied).
test_plan: Unit tests for head activity metrics and compact serialization (CI).
Microbench harness: run streaming bench with real customer traces anonymized (internal cluster).
Regression suite: run sampling-quality checks across 10 canonical prompts, compare token distributions and perplexity.
Load test: 48-hour soak on dedicated node to detect calibration drift and memory leaks.
Canary: staged rollout to 5% of streaming traffic for two enterprise customers with immediate rollback criteria defined.
Chaos test: simulate GPU preemption and network jitter to verify graceful fallback to mixed-precision paths.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Head scale miscalibration leads to numeric instability and quality degradation. Mitigation: conservative thresholds, decay-based rescale, and immediate fallback to FP16 for offending heads.
Risk: Added complexity in scheduler could increase tail latency. Mitigation: keep microbatch scheduling heuristic simple and instrument p99 with alerts; roll out with low traffic first.
Risk: Memory overhead for storing per-head metadata. Mitigation: compact 8-bit exponent encoding, eviction policy for long-tail layers.
Risk: Attack surface where adversarial inputs force thrashing. Mitigation: rate-limit hot-head promotions per-request and per-client, add circuit breaker.
Risk: CI flakiness for kernel numeric checks. Mitigation: broaden tolerance band for stochastic ops and use deterministic seeds where possible.
rollout_plan: Stage 0: internal dev + perf team validation (done).
Stage 1: Canary on internal canary cluster and 1 internal customer (5% traffic) for 72 hours.
Stage 2: Expand to 20% traffic for select streaming customers with runbook on-call.
Stage 3: GA toggle per-tenant with default off, enable via support/eval for customers that opt-in.
Rollback: immediate rollback to mixed-precision if perplexity > 0.02 or p99 latency increases > 20% for the canary group.
